{"version":1,"content":"

HOW TO USE

Turns a folder of pictures into a slideshow video in one Run, no editing program needed. Each picture holds for the seconds you set.

 Pick your folder

  1. On Load Images from Folder Pixaroma, click Browse and pick your folder, or paste the folder's path into the box.
  2. Click Pick images, then Select all, or click only the pictures you want. The button shows how many are picked.
  3. Press Run once. Leave the Run count at 1: the node sends every picture through by itself, one after the other.

This workflow opens with no folder picked: choose your own folder, or try it first on the demo folder Products inside the Media Inputs folder that comes with these workflows.

 A folder inside ComfyUI's own input or output folder works straight away. A folder anywhere else works too, but pick it once with Browse: that is how ComfyUI knows you allowed it.

 Pictures go through in name order. Name them 01_, 02_ and so on if the order matters.

 Set the video

  • 2. seconds per picture and 3. frames per second: the Math node multiplies them for you, so there is no counting to do.
  • 4. video size: 1080 x 1080 for a square post, 1080 x 1920 for a story or a short, 1920 x 1080 for YouTube.
  • Want music? Load Audio Pixaroma can be wired into Save Mp4's audio input, and trim to audio on Save Mp4 cuts the video to the song's length.

 Why the extra nodes

Load Images from Folder sends pictures ONE BY ONE, which is perfect for saving each picture, but a video needs all its frames together. Rebatch Images collects the pieces back into one batch first. Use the same trick whenever you want one result from a whole folder.

 How long it takes

4 pictures, 2 seconds each at 30 fps, 240 frames at 1080 x 1080: 4.7 s on a 4090. No AI model is used.

 Something not working?

Each button opens the answer on the Pixaroma help page.

Save Mp4 says ffmpeg was not found Folder not approved Nodes look different from the video

{"version":1,"content":"

WHAT EACH NODE DOES

The colour of a node tells you what kind of node it is. Nothing here needs changing except the blue ones.

 The steps you set

Blue, and numbered. These are the only nodes you need to touch.

  • Load Images from Folder Pixaroma (1. your folder) - Point it at a folder and pick the pictures. Press Run once and it sends every picture through the workflow, one after the other. Its filename output carries each picture's name to the save node, and index says which picture it is (1, 2, 3 ...).
  • Number Pixaroma (2. seconds per picture) - How many seconds each picture stays on screen.
  • Number Pixaroma (3. frames per second) - Frames per second of the video. 30 is smooth and common; 24 looks like film. The same number goes to the Math node and to Save Mp4.
  • Resize Crop Pixaroma (4. video size) - Makes every picture the video size, here a 1080 x 1080 square, by cropping the edges. A video needs every frame to be the same size.

 The helpers

Purple. They run by themselves and do the small jobs: count, pick, join or pass things along.

  • Math Expression (frames per picture = a x b) - Works out how many frames each picture needs: a * b = seconds per picture x frames per second. 2 x 30 = 60 frames.

 The work

Green. They run by themselves.

  • Repeat Image Batch (holds each picture) - Repeats each picture that many times, so it holds still on screen for the seconds you set.
  • Rebatch Images (all frames into one video) - Joins the frames of every picture into ONE long batch, so the video gets them all at once instead of making one tiny video per picture.

 The result

Dark red, at the end.

  • Save Mp4 Pixaroma (the slideshow) - Turns the frames into an MP4 video and plays it right on the node. It is saved into ComfyUI/output/Slideshow.

 Readouts

Dark. Nothing to set: they show you what happened.

  • Run Timer - The dark clock above the result shows how long the last Run took.
